**Analysis Summary:**

- Test image: elongated pepper/tomato fruit, lower half covered by a dark greenish-black, greasy, water-soaked lesion. Upper half is healthy red. Some whitish growth visible at the lesion base. Fruit still firm/intact.
- Phytophthora_Blight pod: shows collapsed wrinkled peppers — same disease category, different stage
- Anthracnose pod: circular sunken spot with concentric rings — different pattern
- Gray_Mold pod: ghost spots on red tomatoes — no match
- Late_Blight leaf: brown papery lesions — leaf only, but description of fruit symptoms (firm, greasy, dark lesion) closely fits test image
- Bacterial_Canker pod: tiny bird's-eye spots — no match
- TSWV pod: necrotic blotches on green tomatoes — no match
- Rhizopus_Soft_Rots pod: fully collapsed/shriveled fruit — no match
- Verticillium_Wilt leaf: V-shaped yellow lesion — irrelevant

The test image most strongly resembles **Phytophthora_Blight** — the dark, greasy, water-soaked lesion covering the lower fruit half with white material at the base is consistent with P. capsici fruit rot. Late Blight is also possible but Phytophthora_Blight references come from the same Bugwood image collection and the visual pattern matches better.
